comparator.name: American Studies
comparator.route: American Studies — students remaining in the Netherlands
comparator.sourceNotes: Current official prospective pages provide one indicative 2027-intake pathway:2027–2028 year 1 twelve 5 EC compulsory courses (60 EC);2028–2029 year 2 six 5 EC compulsory courses plus two Faculty of Arts minors of 15 EC, one each semester (60 EC);2029–2030 home-study year 3 four 5 EC compulsory courses,10 EC thesis and 30 EC free electives (60 EC). These pages explicitly say provisional, subject to change and no rights derived; they are not future formal regulations. Third-year students remaining in the Netherlands normally take 15 EC of free electives per semester. The abroad route has a different 30 EC specialist/compulsory allocation and is not combined with this pathway. Year 1 RADAr academic language proficiency and mentoring, and year 2 mentorship, are listed at 0 EC and remain additional obligations. The overview gives a 45 of 60 EC first-year positive BSA threshold, subject to personal circumstances. An educational minor is optional, taught in Dutch, and confers a bounded lower-secondary qualification; it is not an automatic outcome of the ordinary BA. No undisclosed thesis-entry threshold is invented.
components: Settler Colonial and North American Indigenous Studies

Two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors, one per semester. Each own-programme additional minor selects three 5 EC courses from its relevant menu; other Faculty language/culture or interdisciplinary minors are also allowed.
Modern and Contemporary North American Literature
Politics and Cultures of the Black Freedom Struggle
Beyond your Bachelor's: English and American Studies Specialist on the Job Market
Required 10 EC bachelor thesis. The prospective overview does not specify a thesis-entry threshold; no new condition is inferred.

30 EC genuine elective space, normally 15 EC per semester on the home-study route. Internship or an optional Dutch-taught educational minor may fill this space. Study abroad uses a different listed third-year pathway.

Complementary primary-source method: a course-filling paper uses diaries, letters and reports about the 1809  Walcheren expedition. This fixed European case teaches historical source analysis; it does not offer unrestricted American-history topic choice or replace a separate bachelor thesis.

studies how media technologies shape the production, circulation and preservation of cultural meaning

Complementary media application: analyses environmental representation using Anthropocene, animal, Indigenous and postcolonial perspectives. It supplies a specific ecological-cultural lens, rather than a general Indigenous-media syllabus.

applies feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority, psychoanalytic and humanist perspectives in an independent literary research project
Direct cultural practice and analysis: poetry, performance, sound and hybrid creative projects examine linguistic and cultural meaning; it does not include singing, songwriting or music performance.

Complementary historiography: examines how art historians from the sixteenth century onward have interpreted art through debates about aesthetics, authorship, identity and global art history; no independent art-research project is promised.

Complementary institutional analysis: compares constitutional and administrative principles in five legal systems, addressing government powers, democracy and rights. The workbook does not identify the five systems; dedicated US constitutional coverage is not assumed.

Complementary global-historical framework: theories and comparative histories of empires and great-power politics support interpretation of United States global influence; no dedicated US-empire syllabus is claimed.
examines the legal, historical and philosophical foundations of rights and their institutional protection
provides concepts of liberty, equality, authority, democracy and political obligation for analysing American political ideas
provides the public-international-law framework for interstate relations, international organisations and global order

Complementary social-conflict application: an international youth-radicalisation project develops evidence-based educational materials about democratic culture, empathy and civic engagement; it is not a course on American extremism.

routeSelection.route: American Studies — students remaining in the Netherlands
routeSelection.basis: Exact target-named American Studies specialisation of the BA English Language and Culture. Use the ordinary home-study third-year pathway rather than the separately listed study-abroad substitution route. Restricted second-year minors and genuine third-year electives remain unfilled choice space, without selecting topics for UCR convenience.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two generator-backed and feasible organising directions: American literature, media and cultural expression; and American politics, identity and global affairs. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The separately evidenced English-teaching direction is not feasible because UCR does not offer a sufficiently complete sequence in English linguistics, language proficiency, second-language pedagogy and supervised teacher preparation.

alternatives.label: American society, politics & culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines American and modern history, political institutions and international relations with sociology, literature, media, art, rhetoric, language and research; the label therefore names its broad social, political and cultural composition.
alternatives.concept: American-focused history and media combine with comparative politics, international relations, sociology, literature, art and rhetoric. Qualitative inquiry, a fixed European historical-source case and psycholinguistics supply complementary research and language perspectives.
progression: Political, rhetorical, cognitive, historical, literary, sociological and media foundations precede advanced work in American Indigenous history, race and media, contemporary social theory, persuasion, art, psycholinguistics and fixed-topic primary-source historical analysis. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

alternatives.label: American literature, media & cultural expression
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around literary interpretation, American and global media, cultural history, visual art, race, rhetoric and creative production, so the label names the three dominant strands.
alternatives.concept: Literature, film, media, art and creative communication organise this cultural route, with American gender history, mainstream media and race providing a substantial United States focus. Comparative literary study and environmental media broaden its interpretive methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Culture and interpretation replace comparative politics, international relations, peace/conflict, psycholinguistics and historical-source work with media archaeology, environmental representation, film adaptation, literary theory, creative communication, documentary and art historiography. 8 courses differ from the broad programme; this is a change of academic emphasis and method.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, modern history, art history, sociology and research methods precede advanced literary theory, film adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication, persuasion and art-fixed-topic primary-source historical analysis. Every course is offered in its assigned term; no selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite.
traceOverrides: examines persuasion, framing, influence and communication ethics as cultural and media practices

alternatives.label: American politics, identity & global affairs
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates political institutions and ideas, constitutional and international law, history, social movements, conflict, identity, race and the United States in global affairs.
alternatives.concept: American-focused history, media and race combine with comparative government, political thought, rights, law and international relations. Civil-society theory, environmental-justice movements and youth-radicalisation research provide specific comparative perspectives on power and social conflict.
alternatives.distinctness: Political institutions, rights, law, empire, social movements and youth radicalisation replace much of the broad programme’s literature, art and language. 8 courses differ from the broad programme and 14 from the cultural programme. American-focused history/media remain the anchor; comparative law is not labelled US constitutional training.
progression: Modern history, comparative politics and Law, Society & Justice precede constitutional and international law; historical, political, sociological and research foundations precede advanced Native American history, race and media, social theory, conflict, social movements and fixed-topic primary-source historical analysis. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

examines American social history, identity and everyday life through mainstream media
directly studies race, systemic racism, resistance and cultural power in American history and life
examines persuasion, framing, influence and communication ethics in political and public discourse

blocks: Modern History situates major political and social developments of the modern era, including the international setting of United States history; it is broader and less American-specific than the comparator sequence.

Histories of Gender directly studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century American life, including slavery, gender and social experience; it covers a focused part of the broader history-and-politics course.
Both directly study settler colonialism and Indigenous North American histories, while the UCR course extends into contemporary Native American life.
Both examine international relations and the geopolitical setting of foreign policy; UCR provides general IR theory rather than a dedicated history of United States foreign relations.

Partial institutional correspondence: constitutional and administrative analysis examines government powers, democracy and rights across five systems. The UCR syllabus does not identify those systems and does not establish dedicated US-government coverage.
UCR has no single scheduled course that provides a dedicated introduction to American Studies as an integrated field.

Both examine race, power, resistance and cultural expression in the United States; UCR's course focuses on media and systemic racism rather than the full political history of the Black freedom struggle.
UCR courses address American memory, race and identity in specific contexts, but no single scheduled course reproduces this dedicated American cultural-memory component.
No scheduled UCR course directly reproduces the dedicated Philosophy of Culture component; cultural interpretation elsewhere provides only partial overlap.
Both introduce close reading and academic interpretation across literary forms and genres.
Both provide advanced literary interpretation and research; UCR is comparative and theoretical rather than a dedicated North American literature course.
Both analyse screen media and popular-cultural forms as systems of meaning, although UCR's course is a general film-and-media introduction rather than an American and British survey.
Both directly examine how media storytelling represents America and shapes understandings of its social history and everyday life.
UCR offers substantial literary study but no dedicated survey of American literature.
Both develop structured written and spoken academic communication; UCR frames those skills through rhetoric and argument.
Both analyse how linguistic choices and context shape meaning; UCR focuses on stylistics rather than the comparator's comparative-pragmatics and information-structure specialism.
Both study language scientifically; UCR provides an advanced psycholinguistic account of processing and acquisition rather than a general structural introduction.
UCR courses are taught and assessed in English, but the selected curriculum contains no dedicated English-language-proficiency writing course.
UCR develops oral communication within substantive courses but does not offer an equivalent English-language-proficiency course.
UCR does not offer a dedicated course in American English phonetics.
UCR's Psycholinguistics studies language processing and acquisition, but it does not reproduce a sociolinguistic course on English as a world language.
Both support reflection on academic development and future study or work; UCR's course is broader personal and professional formation.
The comparator preserves 30 EC of genuine minor choice space.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated American Studies sequence in United States history, politics, literature, media and cultural memory, alongside English linguistics, language proficiency and a required thesis. UCR offers American-focused gender and Indigenous history, media and race, supported by comparative politics, literature, law and social inquiry. Its broader comparative courses do not reproduce the full specialist sequence, English phonetics or American-literature survey. The scheduled historical research seminar uses a fixed European case; optional independent research remains separate from the 24-course programme.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: American Studies is Radboud’s English-taught specialisation within the BA English Language and Culture. It studies the United States through history, politics, literature, media, culture and language, with English proficiency, a thesis and substantial minor and elective space.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three related UCR programmes emphasise society and politics, cultural interpretation, or political institutions and global affairs. All include American-focused study, alongside broader comparative courses. They provide less dedicated American literature and English-language training than Radboud, and the scheduled courses do not replace its separate bachelor thesis.

curriculum.limitation: Radboud labels this prospective 2027-intake pathway provisional and subject to change. Year 2 requires two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors; year 3 retains 30 EC of genuine elective space. RADAr and mentoring are additional zero-credit obligations. The published first-year continuation threshold is 45 of 60 EC, subject to personal circumstances. The optional Dutch-taught educational minor has separate teaching-qualification conditions.
